To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the complex international capacity-building partnership between MIT and Portugal has had a significant impact on Portuguese research in terms of the formation of a new cluster of research institutions and research re- orientation.

complex international capacity building partnerships can lead to the formation of new clusters, and that these partnerships can have a positive effect on the research re-orientation of participants and their home institutions.

complex international capacity building partnerships can have a positive impact on the ‘home’ country in terms cluster formation and research focus, but the impact of such partnerships is difficult to measure, and the impact of the program is not as large as the impact of the individual partnerships within it.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question how complex international partnerships shape research clusters, and the methodological approach we present in this paper can be used to assess the impact on the ‘home country’ of complex international partnerships more adequately in terms of the goals they pursue.

the question of how to evaluate complex capacity-building initiatives more adequately “in their own terms” – and with the question of what this might tell us about their role in the emerging landscape of global research policy and practice.
the impact of complex research partnerships, but also with the methodological challenges of evaluating them adequately.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the MIT Portugal Program has had a significant impact on Portuguese research in the areas of science and engineering and has contributed to cluster formation in the hosting country.
our study provides a novel approach to the evaluation of complex research partnerships, and that this approach is particularly suited to the study of complex research partnerships in their own terms.

our findings indicate that complex partnerships can have a considerable impact on cluster formation and research focus, but that more research is needed to fully understand the conditions and mechanisms of this impact.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the program had a significant impact in terms of cluster development, research re-orientation, and internationalization, but that this impact was not equally distributed across the program partners.

complex international research partnerships can have a positive impact on the ‘receiving’ country in terms cluster formation and research focus, but that this impact is not uniform and that the program architecture matters.

complex international capacity building programs can be an effective policy tool for fostering the formation of domestic research clusters and the re-orientation of research activities, but that the design of these initiatives matters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the evaluation of complex capacity-building partnerships should be more adequately informed by the specificities of their one-of-a kind architectures, goals and impacts.

complex international capacity building partnerships are not only a means to achieve international competitiveness, but also a way to reorient national science and innovation policies in a way that is better suited to the challenges of the 21st century.
complex capacity-building programs can have a major impact on the research system of the ‘hosting country’ in ways that are both idiosyncratically and structurally oriented.
